question: What will the reported change in U.S. total nonfarm payroll employment be for August 2026?
resolution_criterion: This question resolves to the seasonally adjusted change in total nonfarm payroll employment for August 2026, as first reported in the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics "Employment Situation" news release scheduled for 8:30 a.m. Eastern Time on Friday, September 4, 2026, available at https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.nr0.htm . The value is expressed in thousands of jobs: for example, a reported increase of 75,000 jobs resolves as 75, and a decline of 40,000 jobs resolves as -40. Later revisions to the August 2026 figure do not affect resolution; only the value in the initial release counts.
reference_class: US August nonfarm payroll FIRST prints vs. Wall Street consensus, 2011-2025 (15 Augusts, ~11 below consensus), combined with 2026's own monthly first-print trend (3-month avg ~20K, 12-month avg ~34K)
dispersion_basis: SD of NFP first-print surprise vs consensus ~70K in the current regime (2026 first prints spanned -92 to +130; BLS's own 90% CI on the monthly change is +/-136K, i.e. sigma~83K from sampling alone; Kalshi's implied IQR [0,80] gives sigma~59K) -> 70 x 2.56 = 179, rounded to 183
reasoning:
[pooled 3 independent research runs (angles P,P,P): medians 35/42/42 -> 39.67; the narrative below is the P-angle run's own view]
Street consensus for August 2026 NFP is +53 to +58K (Dow Jones 53, Reuters 58, composite 56, private 45), range -25 to +121/140. I start from 2026's cooling trend (3-mo avg ~20K, 12-mo ~34K) rather than the consensus point. Two adjustments: (1) the documented August first-print bias -- below consensus 71% of the past 15 Augusts, averaging -71K when below vs +18K when above; excluding the 2021 outlier the expected surprise is still about -25K; (2) soft August inputs: ADP +38K (weakest since January, below the +48K expected), ISM services employment 47.8 in contraction, Challenger announcements +58% m/m. Offsetting positives: initial claims stayed low at 203-206K, Challenger's August tally was the lowest since 2022, layoff-driven collapse is not visible, and prints tend to mean-revert after a negative month (July -23K). Kalshi's matched contract implied a median near +50 with 25% odds of job losses (priced Sept 1, before the weak ADP); I keep its dispersion but shade the center down to +35 on the August-bias evidence. Distribution is left-skewed: a repeat of February's -92K is more available than a +130K upside print.

question: What will the August 2026 seasonally adjusted change in U.S. government employment be, per the BLS report?
resolution_criterion: This question resolves to the seasonally adjusted over-the-month change in total "Government" employment for August 2026 (i.e., the July 2026 to August 2026 change), in thousands, as shown in Table B-1 of the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics "Employment Situation" news release scheduled for release on September 4, 2026 at 8:30 a.m. ET (https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.t17.htm). The value is computed as the August 2026 seasonally adjusted Government employment level minus the July 2026 seasonally adjusted Government employment level, both from the "Government" total line of Table B-1, expressed in thousands. For example, a decline of 53,000 jobs resolves as -53, and a gain of 12,000 jobs resolves as 12.
reference_class: July-to-August seasonally adjusted over-the-month changes in total Government employment (BLS CES, FRED series USGOVT), 2011-2025, excluding the census-distorted years 2010 and 2020
dispersion_basis: SD of the July->August SA change in total Government employment, 2011-2025 excluding census-distorted 2010 and 2020 (FRED USGOVT), = 40k; 40 x 2.56 = 102. Cross-checked against the last 12 monthly changes (SD ~45 including the Oct-2025 -153 outlier, ~22 excluding it) - August runs roughly 2x a normal month.
reasoning:
[pooled 3 independent research runs (angles P,P,P): medians -7/-10/-2 -> -6.333; the narrative below is the P-angle run's own view]
Reference class: the 14 non-census Jul->Aug SA changes in total Government employment 2011-2025 (FRED USGOVT), mean +9, median +6.5, SD ~40. I adjust that anchor down roughly 15k for the 2026 contraction regime: trailing 12-month mean -26 (-15 ex-October), trailing 6-month -10, negative in 5 of the last 6 months, with Federal still bleeding ~3-5k/month. That lands near -6. Two forces roughly offset around it. Up: the implied Dow Jones consensus (total +53 minus private +47) puts government at about +6, TradingEconomics carries +10, SA local-government-education changes are strongly negatively autocorrelated so July's -49.6k LGE plunge argues for partial reversal, and August government first prints have historically been above their later revisions (Aug 2025 first print -16, now -50) - this question resolves on the first print. Down: the school-district layoff wave is real and structural (7 of the 10 largest districts cutting, ESSER expiry, enrollment decline), so the July drop may persist rather than revert; Labor Day is Sept 7 (latest possible), so fewer school staff are back on payroll by the Aug 12 reference week; ADP was soft; and consensus has been systematically too optimistic in 2026 (July: -23 actual vs +83 consensus). I settle at a median of -7 with wide, mildly left-skewed dispersion. No prediction market prices the Government line specifically - Kalshi KXPAYROLLS-26AUG and Polymarket cover total nonfarm only, a contract mismatch on the quantity being forecast, so I use them only as a read on aggregate tone. Escape masses: 6% above +50 via a full seasonal-factor reversal of the July education drop (cf. Aug 2023 +70, Aug 2021 +97); 1% below -130 requiring an October-2025-scale event (-153, mass federal separations) recurring in August.

question: How many named storms will the 2026 Atlantic hurricane season have had by September 5, 2026?
resolution_criterion: This question asks for the cumulative number of named tropical storms in the 2026 Atlantic hurricane season that had formed on or before September 5, 2026 (i.e. that were assigned a name from the Atlantic naming list at any point through that date). It resolves based on the National Hurricane Center's 2026 Atlantic Hurricane Season summary table at https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/data/tcr/index.php?season=2026&basin=atl — specifically, the count of distinct named systems (those listed with a name such as Arthur, Bertha, etc.) whose first attainment of tropical-storm or subtropical-storm status (the start of the "Dates active" range) fell on or before September 5, 2026 (UTC). A system is counted if it was named on or before September 5, 2026, regardless of its later intensity (a system that strengthened into a hurricane still counts as one named storm). For example, if six named systems had formed through September 5, the question resolves as 6.
reference_class: Cumulative Atlantic named-storm counts as of September 5 in past seasons (1991-2020 climatology, ~7 by this date), superseded by the directly observed 2026 count in the named resolution source
dispersion_basis: Near-degenerate: 5 storms are already on the books and the NHC 7-day outlook (00:00Z Sep 4) shows zero disturbance areas with 'formation not expected during the next 7 days'. Conditional on a no-areas 7-day TWO, genesis inside the remaining ~24h to resolution is well under 1%, so the true 10th and 90th percentiles are both exactly 5; 0.35 is a floor-respecting minimum spread, not a claim of real uncertainty.
reasoning:
[pooled 3 independent research runs (angles P,P,P): medians 5/5/5 -> 5; the narrative below is the P-angle run's own view]
Reference class anchor: the Atlantic averages ~7 named storms by Sep 5 (1991-2020 climatology), which is where a blind prior would sit. That prior is fully superseded by direct observation of the resolution source. The NHC 2026 season table lists exactly five named systems with genesis dates on or before Sep 5: Arthur (17 Jun), Bertha (19 Jul), Cristobal (12 Aug), Dolly (27 Aug), Edouard (31 Aug). Two independent Sep 2-3 news reports corroborate five named storms and zero hurricanes, attributing the suppressed season to a very strong El Nino (high shear); NOAA holds a 75% below-normal call and CSU cut its full-season total from 13 to 9. The question is effectively already resolved: the only path to 6 is a named system forming between 00:00Z Sep 4 and resolution, and the 8 PM EDT Sep 3 TWO carries no disturbance areas and an explicit 'not expected during the next 7 days'. I price P(6) at roughly 1% (allowing for a surprise subtropical low and for the criteria text arguably extending the window through end-of-day Sep 5), P(5) at ~99%. Contamination note: one web-search summary asserted 12 named storms by late August; it conflicts with the primary NHC table and was discarded.
what_would_change_my_mind: A new Atlantic invest or disturbance area appearing in an NHC TWO with a non-trivial 48-hour formation chance before 2026-09-05T00:00Z
The NHC season table adding a sixth named system, or a satellite-flagged subtropical low being named without prior TWO warning
Evidence that the resolution window is read as running through end-of-day Sep 5 UTC AND a fast-developing system appearing in that extra 24 hours

question: How many waterbodies will be on the Massachusetts DPH harmful cyanobacterial bloom advisory list on September 4, 2026?
resolution_criterion: This question resolves as the number of distinct waterbodies listed under the "Current List of Waterbodies" section of the Massachusetts Department of Public Health "Harmful Cyanobacterial Bloom Advisories in Massachusetts" page (https://www.mass.gov/info-details/harmful-cyanobacterial-bloom-advisories-in-massachusetts) on the version of the page that is "current as of" a date falling on or after August 31, 2026 and on or before September 4, 2026. Each bulleted waterbody entry counts as one, exactly as the page enumerates them (for example, the version current as of August 21, 2026 listed 25 entries, which would resolve as 25). If multiple dated versions qualify, use the one whose "current as of" date is closest to and not after September 4, 2026.
reference_class: Early-September (Aug 31-Sep 7) versions of the MA DPH 'Harmful Cyanobacterial Bloom Advisories' list, 2023-2025 seasons, plus the same-season within-week persistence of the posted 'current as of' version
dispersion_basis: Mixture over a ~3-day horizon: ~2/3 chance the Sept 1 version (31 entries) is still the current one at the Sept 4 check (2026 update gaps observed: 6 and 5 days); conditional on a Sept 2-4 update, SD of 3-day changes in this list ~2.5 (the list moved 25 -> 31 over 11 days, Aug 21 -> Sep 1), giving a mixture 10-90 width of roughly 4.
reasoning:
[pooled 3 independent research runs (angles P,P,P): medians 31/31/31 -> 31; the narrative below is the P-angle run's own view]
The question is very nearly already resolved: the qualifying version exists. The live mass.gov page is 'current as of September 1, 2026' and enumerates 31 waterbodies (Charles River Lower Basin, Cliff/Walkers Ponds Brewster, Chicopee Reservoir, three Chilmark/Tisbury ponds, six Plymouth ponds, Indian Lake Worcester, etc.), and mass.gov/lists/algae-information independently shows the advisory 'Updated September 1, 2026'. Under the criterion, Sept 1 falls in the Aug 31-Sep 4 window, so 31 resolves unless DPH posts a newer version dated Sept 2-4 before the check. 2026 cadence (Aug 21 -> Aug 27 -> Sep 1) implies the next refresh lands ~Sept 6-8; I price ~1/3 on an earlier Fri Sept 4 (pre-Labor-Day) post. Conditional on such an update, the seasonal trend is still upward (25 -> 31 in 11 days; 2025 climbed ~27 to ~40 across the same span), so I skew the conditional mass slightly above 31 (mode 32-33). Residual low-side mass covers a possible off-by-one in my parse of the bulleted list (e.g. the Charles River being split into two reaches, as it was on Aug 21). Evidence is direct-observation-strong, not thin; the spread is small because the status quo is already the answer.
what_would_change_my_mind: A new 'current as of' version dated Sept 2, 3 or 4 appearing on the page before Sept 4 20:00 EDT
Evidence that DPH posts updates on a fixed Friday schedule (which would make a Sept 4 version near-certain)
A recount of the Sept 1 page showing a different number of bullets (e.g. the Charles River split into two reaches, or sub-bullets counted separately)
A large multi-town advisory wave (Cape Cod / Plymouth cluster) reported Sept 2-3 that DPH would fold into a rushed update

sources: WebSearch site:mass.gov enumeration of dated 'current as of' alert pages (Jul 3/16/29/30, Aug 19, Oct 6/10, Dec 3 2025) used for update cadence

question: How many of the four vessels held by Somali pirates (HONOUR 25, SWARD, EUREKA, ASANA) will still be under pirate control on September 5, 2026?
resolution_criterion: This question resolves as the number of the following four merchant vessels — HONOUR 25 (Palau-flagged product tanker), SWARD (Saint Kitts and Nevis-flagged cargo vessel), EUREKA (Togo-flagged tanker), and ASANA (Tanzania-flagged tanker, also rendered ASNA) — that remain under Somali pirate control as of September 5, 2026, according to EU NAVFOR Operation Atalanta. A vessel is counted as still under pirate control if, as of September 5, 2026, Atalanta has NOT publicly announced its release/liberation (or the release of its crew) via its newsroom (https://www.eunavfor.eu/news) or official social media. A vessel is counted as released (and therefore NOT included in the total) once Atalanta reports the ship and/or its crew have been freed, whether by ransom, naval action, negotiation, or any other means. For example, if Atalanta has announced the release of EUREKA but the other three remain held, this resolves as 3. If Atalanta's newsroom is unavailable, resolution may rely on credible sources (https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) reporting Atalanta's status of these vessels.
reference_class: Merchant vessels held for ransom by Somali pirate groups that have already been in captivity 6+ weeks, evaluated over a single 24-hour window (2008-2012 wave plus the 2024-2026 resurgence), where median captivity runs 4-6 months
dispersion_basis: Near-degenerate discrete outcome: per-vessel daily release hazard ~0.5-1% (median Somali ransom captivity 4-6 months) implies ~3-4% chance any of the 4 is released AND announced in the remaining ~24h, so the honest 10-90 interval is effectively a point at 4; the 0.45 width is the minimum smear required by the strictly-increasing-percentile constraint and already over-states real dispersion.
reasoning:
[pooled 3 independent research runs (angles P,P,P): medians 4/4.02/3.985 -> 4.002; the narrative below is the P-angle run's own view]
Only ~24h remain (now 2026-09-03T23:52Z to 2026-09-05T00:00Z). Atalanta's newsroom shows no liberation notice for any of the four; its latest relevant post (29 Jul 2026) lists all four as ongoing incidents, and Wikipedia's 27 Aug update and Maritime Executive (31 Jul) both report four vessels / 67 crew still held with no negotiation progress. Two 3 Sep 2026 reports (Masrawy, Asharq Al-Awsat) confirm EUREKA is still held at day 133 with Egyptian diplomacy ongoing and ransom talks stalled/escalated. Base rate: for Somali ransom hijackings past 6 weeks, the daily release hazard is ~0.5-1% per vessel, so ~3% expected releases across 4 vessels in one day; the criterion further requires a public Atalanta announcement, and Atalanta's cadence is roughly monthly, adding lag friction that biases toward 4. Naval rescue is constrained by Somali territorial waters and Atalanta's stated dependence on local authorities. No prediction market prices this (checked Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold - none found), so no crowd anchor. P(4)~0.95, P(3)~0.04, P(<=2)~0.01.

question: Will WHO or Africa CDC report more than 10,000 people vaccinated with Ervebo in the 2026 DRC Bundibugyo Ebola response before September 4, 2026?
resolution_criterion: This question resolves YES if, before 23:59 UTC on September 3, 2026, the World Health Organization (WHO) or the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) publishes a report stating that more than 10,000 people have cumulatively received the Ervebo (rVSV-ZEBOV-GP) vaccine as part of the response to the 2026 Ebola disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo caused by Bundibugyo virus (declared 15 May 2026). Eligible publications include WHO Disease Outbreak News (https://www.who.int/emergencies/disease-outbreak-news), WHO Regional Office for Africa outbreak bulletins, and Africa CDC situation reports/dashboards. The figure must refer to people vaccinated (or doses administered, since Ervebo is a single-dose vaccine), not doses allocated, released, delivered, or pre-positioned. It resolves NO if no such report puts the cumulative figure above 10,000 by that time.
reference_class: WHO/Africa CDC emergency Ervebo campaigns in DRC: time from campaign launch to a published cumulative 'people vaccinated' figure exceeding 10,000 (2018-20 North Kivu launched 8 Aug 2018, crossed ~10,000 reported around late Sept 2018 ~6-7 weeks in; 2020 Equateur peaked ~40,000 over months; 2025 Kasai reached 47,500+ over months). None crossed 10,000 reported within 7 days of launch.
reasoning:
[pooled 3 independent research runs (angles P,P,P) [0.02, 0.03, 0.02] -> 0.023; the narrative below is the P-angle run's own view (0.02)]
This resolves at 2026-09-03T23:59Z, ~15 seconds after the anchor time, so it is a check-the-record question, not a forecast. The record: WHO DON 2026-DON616 states only that 'On 27 August, vaccination of health care workers using the Ervebo vaccine was initiated... including in Kisangani, Tshopo province' — no count. WHO's DRC-2026 emergency situation page and the 20 Aug WHO/Africa CDC joint statement give allocations (70,000: 20k trial + 50k frontline) and deliveries (16,250-16,520 doses landed in Kinshasa 21-22 Aug), all of which the fine print explicitly excludes. Coverage dated 2-3 Sep (n-tv, The Conversation) still quotes 'over 16,000 delivered' and the 70,000 allocation, i.e. no administered figure had surfaced hours before the deadline. Feasibility also cuts NO: the campaign is ~7 days old, in-country supply at launch was ~16.5k doses, and >10,000 administered would mean consuming most of it in a week across insecure Tshopo/Bas-Uele/Haut-Uele health zones — faster than any DRC precedent, and official cumulative counts lag administration anyway. Markets: no human market prices this contract; Polymarket has only 'Ebola pandemic in 2026' (~7.5% YES), a different event (pandemic declaration, not a vaccination-count publication) with no shared threshold, deadline or resolution source — evidence, not an anchor. Residual probability is almost entirely the chance an AFRO weekly bulletin or Africa CDC dashboard published today carried such a figure that four searches missed.
what_would_change_my_mind: A WHO AFRO outbreak bulletin or Africa CDC situation report/dashboard timestamped on or before 2026-09-03 23:59 UTC giving a single cumulative figure above 10,000 people vaccinated or doses administered in the Bundibugyo response
Credible reporting explicitly attributing a >10,000 vaccinated figure to WHO or Africa CDC and dated before the deadline
Evidence that the Phase 3 trial plus frontline campaign enrolled/vaccinated at a rate far above the ~16.5k doses initially in country during 27 Aug-3 Sep

question: Will the FAA authorize SpaceX's Starship reentry trajectory to Starbase before September 4, 2026?
resolution_criterion: This question resolves YES if, as of September 4, 2026 (00:00 UTC), the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has issued a modification to SpaceX's Starship/Super Heavy vehicle operator license (License No. VOL 23-129) that authorizes an additional Starship reentry/landing trajectory returning to the Boca Chica (Starbase, Texas) launch site — the regulatory step required for a Mechazilla tower catch of the Starship upper stage. Any such license modification issued and still in effect at any time before September 4, 2026 (00:00 UTC) counts. It resolves NO otherwise. Resolution is based on the FAA's SpaceX Starship stakeholder page (https://www.faa.gov/space/stakeholder_engagement/spacex_starship) showing an issued license modification (not merely a completed environmental review), or on confirmation from [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) that the FAA has granted such a license modification.
reference_class: US federal licensing actions where the environmental/NEPA step is complete but the discretionary license issuance remains pending, evaluated at the moment a fixed deadline closes with the agency's own docket showing no issuance
reasoning:
[pooled 3 independent research runs (angles P,P,P) [0.12, 0.06, 0.07] -> 0.080; the narrative below is the P-angle run's own view (0.12)]
Deadline is effectively now (00:04Z vs 00:00Z window close), so this is an already-resolved check, not a forecast of future agency action. The Sept 3, 2026 FAA action reported as 'approving the landing catch' is, on the FAA's own words quoted by Spaceflight Now, completion of the environmental review process (Final Tiered EA + FONSI/ROD) for the Pacific contingency areas plus an additional Boca Chica reentry trajectory - exactly what the fine print says does NOT count. The designated resolution source (faa.gov stakeholder page) lists only EA/FONSI/ROD documents, with no 2026 entry announcing issuance of a modification to VOL 23-129, and carries the standard disclaimer that NEPA completion does not guarantee a license modification. Decisive precedent: the RTLS-profile FONSI/ROD was signed 2026-02-12 and the license modification was still 'under evaluation' as of Aug 21, 2026 - the 14 CFR 450 safety review, not NEPA, is the binding constraint, and there is no operational urgency because Flight 14 (NET Sept 15) splashes down and the catch is deferred months. Residual YES probability covers (a) a same-day bundled license modification actually being signed Sept 3 before 19:00 CDT, some outlets claiming SpaceX 'now has the FAA license' for Flight 14, and (b) a resolver conflating the widely-headlined 'FAA approves the catch' coverage with license issuance. No prediction market prices this contract: Polymarket and Kalshi list only Starship launch-count markets for 2026, no Manifold or bookmaker equivalent found, so no anchor.
what_would_change_my_mind: The FAA stakeholder page or activity archive showing a dated entry (on or before 2026-09-03) stating a modification to VOL 23-129 was issued authorizing the Boca Chica reentry trajectory
A tier-1 outlet (SpaceNews, Ars Technica, Spaceflight Now in its own words) reporting explicitly that the FAA 'issued a license modification', not that it 'completed the environmental review'
The full FAA statement of Sept 3 containing a sentence announcing license issuance rather than the standard 'does not guarantee a license modification' disclaimer
Evidence SpaceX reinstated an RTLS/catch profile for Flight 14, which would imply the licensing step was already cleared

question: What will be the cumulative net flow into US spot Bitcoin ETFs over September 1–4, 2026?
resolution_criterion: This question resolves based on the "Total" row of the US Bitcoin ETF flow table published by Farside Investors at https://farside.co.uk/btc/ . It resolves as the sum of the daily "Total" net flow values (in US$ millions) reported for the four trading days 1, 2, 3, and 4 September 2026, expressed in millions of US dollars. For example, if the four daily totals are +150.0, -50.0, +200.0, and +100.0, the sum is +400.0 and the question resolves as 400. Positive values denote net inflows and negative values denote net outflows. If Farside does not report a value for a given day (e.g. a market holiday), that day contributes 0. If Farside Investors is permanently unavailable, an equivalent aggregate from another public US spot Bitcoin ETF flow tracker (e.g. SoSoValue) covering the same four days will be used.
reference_class: Cumulative 4-trading-day sums of the Farside 'Total' row for US spot Bitcoin ETF net flows, 2025-2026, with the first two days of this window already known
dispersion_basis: SD of daily Farside Total flows over the last ~2 months ≈ 240 (Aug 24–Sep 2 sample: +337.6, +314.4, +232.1, +242.2, -201.8, +216.7, -236.5, +101.1; sample SD 224, widened for 2026's fatter tails); two unknown days with ~0.25 autocorrelation → 2-day SD ≈ 380, x2.56 ≈ 975, thinned to ~860 by the 35% branch in which Sep 4 is unpublished at resolution and contributes 0
reasoning:
[pooled 3 independent research runs (angles P,P,P): medians -19/90/95 -> 55.33; the narrative below is the P-angle run's own view]
Two of four days are already observed and published: Sep 1 = -236.5 and Sep 2 = +101.1 (Farside, corroborated by TFTC and SoSoValue), so the sum is anchored at -135.4 with only Sep 3 and Sep 4 unknown. Reference class (4-day sums of Farside Totals over the trailing year) implies a median around +200, but conditioning on the observed -135 start moves the center to roughly zero. Each remaining day I center near +75 (below August's +167/day average, because BTC has fallen from >$80k to ~$77.8k, the Sep 3 session was mildly negative, and the flow regime has flipped to alternating large in/outflows) with SD ~240. Sep 3's flows had not been published anywhere as of 2026-09-04T00:15Z. A live resolution risk: Farside posts day D roughly on D+1, so at the scheduled 2026-09-05T00:00Z read the Sep 4 row is likely still blank and the fine print scores a missing day as 0 — I weight that branch 35%, which pulls the median slightly negative and trims the upper tail. No human prediction market prices this contract (checked Polymarket, Kalshi, bookmakers — none found). Escape below -1000 needs ~-430M/day for two days, near record-redemption territory, so priced at 1%; the upper escape needs two consecutive all-time-record inflow days and is left undeclared.

question: What will the most recent WHO Disease Outbreak News report as the cumulative confirmed Ebola deaths in the DRC, as of September 4, 2026?
resolution_criterion: This question resolves to the number of cumulative confirmed deaths in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) reported in the most recently published WHO Disease Outbreak News (DON) item concerning the ongoing Ebola disease outbreak caused by Bundibugyo virus, as that item appears on the WHO Disease Outbreak News repository (https://www.who.int/emergencies/disease-outbreak-news) as of 23:59 UTC on September 3, 2026. The figure used is the cumulative number of confirmed deaths in the DRC (not the multi-country outbreak total, and not probable/suspected deaths). For example, if the latest DON states "4,665 confirmed cases and 2,184 deaths" in the DRC, this resolves as 2184.
reference_class: Standing WHO Disease Outbreak News figures for this outbreak, given the observed DON publication cadence (~14 days: 1 Aug, 14 Aug, 28 Aug) and ~2-day data lag - i.e. the class of 'what number is the most recent DON showing at an arbitrary instant', which is the last published DON's figure roughly 12 of every 14 days rather than a current-surveillance number
dispersion_basis: Not a forecast of a moving series: the quantity is an already-published number verified directly (DON616, 28 Aug 2026 = 2786 DRC confirmed deaths), and the resolution instant has passed. Residual dispersion is entirely the ~10% chance a DON published 29 Aug-3 Sept was missed by my three checks; such a DON (data ~1 Sept, 2-day lag, confirmed-only) would report roughly 2,950-3,150 given national INSP figures of 3,007 on 31 Aug and 3,039 on 1 Sept. That two-point mixture gives a 10-90 width near 190, not the reference-class width of a live epidemic count.
reasoning:
[pooled 3 independent research runs (angles P,P,P): medians 2786/2786/2786 -> 2786; the narrative below is the P-angle run's own view]
Resolution is the DRC-only confirmed-death figure in the most recent WHO DON as of 23:59 UTC 3 Sep 2026. WHO DON 2026-DON616, published 28 Aug (data as of 26 Aug), states 5794 confirmed cases including 2786 deaths for the DRC (CFR 48.1%); its multi-country paragraph gives 5815 cases / 2788 deaths including two in Uganda, confirming 2786 is the DRC-only count and matching the criteria's example format. No later DON exists: 2026-DON617 and 2026-DON618 both 404 (ids increment across all diseases), and ECDC's outbreak page, last updated 3 Sep 15:10, cites no WHO DON after 28 Aug. Cadence for this outbreak is ~14 days (DON614 1 Aug/data 30 Jul; DON615 14 Aug/data 12 Aug; DON616 28 Aug/data 26 Aug), placing the next item around 11 Sep - after the resolution instant. Much higher national INSP figures (6,186/3,007 as of 31 Aug; 6,250/3,039 as of 1 Sep) are widely reported but are explicitly not the DON and do not resolve this; they are the main trap. No human prediction market prices this contract (Polymarket's Ebola books are on emergency declaration, country spread, and a 2026 pandemic definition ~7.5%, none on a DON death count), so no market anchor is applied. Both bounds left unpriced: even the missed-DON branch lands ~3,050, well inside 2100-3800.
